title: Shell injection via ${{ github.event.label.name }} interpolation in pull_request_target run: bodies (add-ci-passed-label.yml, ci-checks.yml)
Missing authorization on v1alpha1 run-log HTTP endpoint allows cross-namespace pod log disclosure in multi-user mode — new PR filed
Missing authorization on v1beta1 TaskService (CreateTaskV1 + ListTasksV1) allows cross-tenant task disclosure and execution-cache poisoning — covered by in-flight PR
Path traversal via key param in /artifacts/get?source=volume lets any authenticated user read arbitrary files (e.g. SA token) from ml-pipeline-ui pod — covered by in-flight PR
Missing authorization on HTTP pipeline upload/upload_version lets any multi-user tenant create and overwrite shared (empty-namespace) pipelines that all namespaces run — filed, PR to open manually

Code injection / RCE in visualization service via unsanitized `source` string-formatted into an executed notebook cell (VisualizationService.CreateVisualization), reachable cross-tenant via the empty-namespace authorization skip

TensorBoard proxy HMAC signing key defaults to the object-store credential MINIO_SECRET_KEY (public default `minio123`), making proxy tokens forgeable — unauthenticated in-cluster SSRF to arbitrary <label>-service.<label>.svc.cluster.local:80 in default standalone mode (frontend/server/configs.ts)
Decompression bomb in pipeline archive upload (unbounded io.ReadAll on decompressed .tar.gz/.zip) can OOM the API server (DoS) in backend/src/apiserver/server/util.go

SSRF via http/https artifact source: ml-pipeline-ui artifact proxy fetches an attacker-chosen single-label in-cluster host because ALLOWED_ARTIFACT_DOMAIN_REGEX defaults to allow-all (^.*$) and bucket becomes the host when HTTP_BASE_URL is empty; unauthenticated in standalone (frontend/server/handlers/artifacts.ts) — filed, PR to open manually

Arbitrary code execution via eval() of attacker-controlled dsl.Condition (triggerPolicy.condition) in the kfp.local enhanced DAG orchestrator; escapes DockerRunner container isolation when running an untrusted pipeline locally

SSRF via attacker-controlled s3/minio providerInfo.endpoint on /artifacts/get: full host:port outbound fetch (incl. 169.254.169.254 and arbitrary ports) bypasses the artifact domain allowlist that only guards http/https; unauthenticated in default standalone (frontend/server/handlers/artifacts.ts)

Missing authorization on CreateVisualizationV1: an empty request namespace skips the IsAuthorized SubjectAccessReview in multi-user mode and routes the attacker-controlled visualization request to the shared system-namespace visualization service

Stored XSS: pipeline version code_source_url rendered unsanitized into an anchor href (Version source link) in PipelineVersionCard / PipelineDetailsV1; any upload-capable user plants a non-http(s) (e.g. javascript:) scheme that executes in the ml-pipeline-ui origin on click — filed fork PR, upstream via private channel

Cross-tenant archived pod-log disclosure: ml-pipeline-ui archive object key (createPodLogsMinioRequestConfig) is derived from caller-supplied podname/createdat and is not scoped to the authorized podnamespace, so an authenticated tenant can read another tenant's archived pod logs from the shared bucket in multi-user mode when ARGO_ARCHIVE_LOGS is enabled

SSRF via unvalidated, tenant-influenced Argo artifact-repository s3.endpoint in the ml-pipeline-ui pod-log archive fallback (getPodLogsMinioRequestConfigfromWorkflow): a namespace-owning multi-user tenant seeds a namespace-local artifact-repositories configmap so the resolved workflow-status endpoint points at an attacker host:port, and the shared frontend builds an object-store client toward it and streams the response back (also leaks the object-store access-key ID) — filed fork PR, upstream via private channel

Reflected XSS in ml-pipeline-ui /artifacts/get: attacker-controlled `key` query param reflected unescaped into text/html 404 bodies (No objects found at {bucket}/{key}) in the MinIO directory-fallback paths, executing script in the KFP UI origin

Un-namespaced /ml_metadata.* gRPC-web proxy in frontend server exposes cross-tenant MLMD metadata (artifact URIs, run params/metrics, pipeline names) in multi-user mode — KNOWN/ACCEPTED upstream limitation (issue #4790); MLMD has no tenancy model and no minimal fix exists, so not filed as a PR

Missing authorization on the referenced pipeline version during run/recurring-run creation lets a multi-user tenant embed and execute another namespace's private pipeline by referencing its version UUID (cross-tenant IDOR); disclosure of the private pipeline spec via read-back — reviewed fork PR open, upstream PR to open manually

Arbitrary host-file disclosure escaping DockerRunner isolation via dsl.importer(download_to_workspace=True) with a file:// or bare-path artifact_uri: the host-side importer (importer_handler._copy_local_artifact_to_workspace) copies an arbitrary host path into the container-mounted workspace, readable by untrusted task code; same untrusted-local-pipeline + DockerRunner precondition as the already-filed dsl.Condition eval RCE — recorded, no separate fix (gray-area/subsumed, no clean fix without changing download_to_workspace semantics)

Cross-tenant execution-cache read and poisoning: the v1 cache mutating webhook computes a namespace-agnostic cache key (generateCacheKeyFromTemplate) and GetExecutionCache matches on that key alone, while the MutatingWebhookConfiguration has no namespaceSelector — in multi-user mode a tenant can read another tenant's cached ExecutionOutput and poison shared cachedb entries other tenants consume (legacy v1 path only; v2 driver cache is namespace-scoped)

Stored XSS in ml-pipeline-ui artifact proxy: /artifacts/get serves raw, user-controlled artifact bytes inline with a renderable/MIME-sniffable Content-Type (res.send() defaults to text/html for GCS; minio/s3/http/volume pipe with no Content-Type) and no nosniff/Content-Disposition/CSP, so an HTML/script artifact opened via the same-origin "View" link executes in the ml-pipeline-ui session; distinct from the reflected key-error XSS and the code_source_url href XSS

Privilege escalation via unsanitized TensorBoard Viewer podTemplateSpec: the viewer controller renders a tenant-supplied v1.PodTemplateSpec into a Deployment verbatim (only Containers[0] name/image/args/ports overwritten), letting any namespace user with create on viewers.kubeflow.org request hostPath volumes, privileged/capability containers, host namespaces, or an arbitrary serviceAccountName — node breakout / cross-identity escalation bypassing pipeline pod PSS hardening; no validating webhook

Cross-namespace workflow counting in the multi-user ScheduledWorkflow controller: WorkflowClient.List/ExecutionInformer.List count active/completed Argo Workflows by label selector only with no namespace scope, so a tenant's decoy workflows (bearing the scheduledWorkflowName/workflowIndex labels) count against another namespace's schedule and, via the maxConcurrency gate (default 1), starve the victim's recurring runs (plus foreign metadata written into the victim's ScheduledWorkflow status)

Cross-tenant run-record tampering: the API server updates a run selected solely by the attacker-settable pipelines.kubeflow.org/runid label on a workflow reported by the cluster-wide persistence agent, with no namespace match, letting a tenant overwrite another tenant's run state and stored runtime manifest

Reflected XSS in ml-pipeline-ui TensorBoard create handler: the caller-supplied logdir query param is echoed unescaped into a text/html 500 error body (POST /apps/tensorboard), executing script in the UI origin via an auto-submitting cross-site form against a logged-in user

Cross-tenant run execution via the multi-user ScheduledWorkflow controller: a tenant with kubeflow-edit can create a ScheduledWorkflow directly in their own namespace pointing ExperimentId at another namespace, and the cluster-privileged controller creates/executes a run in the victim namespace (bypasses API-server per-user authz)

Cross-tenant object-store artifact disclosure in the v2 launcher: fetchNonDefaultBuckets lends the run's default (shared) object-store session to an author-controlled input-artifact URI (e.g. a dsl.importer artifact_uri stored verbatim in MLMD) that resolves to the same bucket but outside this run's pipeline-root prefix, so a multi-user tenant isolated by per-namespace object-store prefix can read another prefix's artifacts with the shared credentials via DownloadBlob prefix listing — fork PR #129 closed unmerged by repo owner after assessment (issue NOT fixed; feature branch retained), upstream via private channel (SECURITY.md)

Stored XSS in ml-pipeline-ui pod-info endpoints: /k8s/pod and /k8s/pod/events return Kubernetes objects via res.send(JSON.stringify(...)), which Express serves as text/html with no nosniff/CSP, so attacker-influenced pod fields (annotations/labels/container args/env) render as script in the ml-pipeline-ui origin when a namespace-authorized victim navigates to the pod-info URL — reviewed fork PR open, upstream via private channel (SECURITY.md)

ServiceAccount authorization bypass on run/recurring-run creation: only the workflow-level spec.serviceAccountName is authorized, so a user-supplied v1 Argo workflow manifest can pin a privileged account via templates[].serviceAccountName, templateDefaults, executor, artifactGC or podSpecPatch, which Argo prefers over it — bypassing both ALLOWEDSERVICEACCOUNTS and the 'use' SubjectAccessReview

Workflow-run approval gate ignores needs-ok-to-test: gh-workflow-approve.yml auto-approves fork pull_request runs on any ok-to-test PR, including after a maintainer revokes trust with needs-ok-to-test and across unreviewed force-pushes

GCP access-token exposure in kfp.Client: _is_inverse_proxy_host uses an unanchored, unescaped regex (\S+.googleusercontent.com/{0,1}$) so look-alike, path-carrying, or userinfo-carrying endpoints trigger the implicit Application Default Credentials token exchange and receive the caller's cloud-platform-scoped Bearer token - fork PR open, upstream via private channel (SECURITY.md)

GCE access-token and identity-token disclosure via pod logs: proxy/attempt-register-vm-on-proxy.sh runs under set -ex and the registration curl expands $(gcloud auth print-access-token) and ${VM_ID} on its command line, so bash xtrace writes the live Bearer token to the proxy-agent container log readable by any pods/log reader or log-pipeline consumer (GKE Cloud Logging) - fork PR open, upstream via private channel (SECURITY.md)

Cross-tenant run disclosure via caller-chosen run id: CreateRun/CreateRunV1 keep the request's run_id (toModelRun -> ResourceManager.CreateRun only generates when empty) and RunStore.CreateRun resolves the resulting primary-key collision through the recurring-run idempotency branch by returning GetRun(uuid) with no namespace or recurring-run match, so a multi-user tenant with their own recurring run receives another namespace's run record (params, manifest, state) - fork PR open, upstream via private channel (SECURITY.md)

Cross-tenant pipeline metadata disclosure via by-name lookup: PipelineStore.GetPipelineByNameAndNamespace[V1] omit the Namespace predicate when the namespace is empty and getPipelineByName skips the SubjectAccessReview for an empty-namespace get, so an authenticated multi-user tenant calling GetPipelineByName without a namespace receives the newest ready pipeline of that name from any namespace (UUID, namespace, description, tags; v1 also latest-version parameters and code_source_url) - fixed upstream by kubeflow/pipelines#14522 (v2 lookup) and #14478 (v1 API removed); fork PR #144 closed as superseded

CI-gate bypass via spoofed workflow_run: add-ci-passed-label.yml is triggered by workflow_run on any completed workflow *named* "CI Check" and applies the ci-passed label from that run's ci-check-result artifact without verifying the triggering workflow path (.github/workflows/ci-checks.yml) or event (pull_request_target), so an ok-to-test fork PR that adds its own workflow named CI Check can self-award ci-passed with a crafted artifact - issue and branch filed by the 2026-09-13 run, fork PR #146 opened 2026-09-15 then closed 2026-09-26 as superseded: upstream #14552 (610a06339) deleted add-ci-passed-label.yml and moved ci-passed into ci-checks.yml as a SHA-bound status publisher that verifies expected workflows by trusted path/inventory, closing this path

Unauthenticated SeaweedFS credential minting via the multi-user profile-controller sync webhook: pipelines-profile-controller/sync.py serves the metacontroller sync hook over plain HTTP with no authentication, trusts object.metadata.name from the request body, calls iam.create_access_key/put_user_policy for that namespace with the controller's root object-store credentials and returns the new access key and secret in the response; the pod has no Istio sidecar and no NetworkPolicy, so any tenant pod can POST to kubeflow-pipelines-profile-controller.kubeflow/sync naming a victim namespace and obtain credentials for its private-artifacts/private prefixes - fork PR open, upstream via private channel (SECURITY.md)
notes: 2026-09-26: fix branch rebased onto fork master 89594c6d4 (head 4f998a9ef) so the new SHA-bound ci-passed gate evaluates a current head; PR #148 still open.

title: Local credential exposure in kfp.Client: auth.get_auth_token persists the IAP OAuth refresh token together with the OAuth client id and client secret to ~/.config/kfp/credentials.json (and set_user_namespace persists the context file that can carry client authentication cookies/headers) using os.makedirs and open('w') with process-default permissions (0755/0644) and no chmod, so any other local user or process able to read the home directory obtains a long-lived refresh token plus the client secret and can mint IAP ID tokens as the victim - fork PR open, upstream via private channel (SECURITY.md)

Cross-tenant object-store read via tenant-authored Workflow status in the ml-pipeline-ui pod-log fallback: getPodLogsMinioRequestConfigfromWorkflow takes the bucket (status.artifactRepositoryRef.artifactRepository.s3.bucket) and the main-logs object key (status.nodes[<pod>].outputs.artifacts[].s3.key) verbatim from the Argo Workflow status, which a tenant with the edit role can write because the Workflow CRD has no status subresource, and for a user-namespace run fetches that object with the frontend's shared MINIO_ACCESS_KEY/MINIO_SECRET_KEY, so GET /k8s/pod/logs?podname=<crafted-workflow>&podnamespace=<own-ns> returns any object those credentials reach (other namespaces' private-artifacts/<ns>/ artifacts and archived logs); the endpoint allow-list from the earlier SSRF fix does not apply because the attacker names the trusted store - fork PR open, upstream via private channel (SECURITY.md)

Unbounded in-memory buffering in the ml-pipeline-ui GCS artifact handler: getGCSArtifactHandler lists every object under the caller-chosen key prefix and readGCSObject/Buffer.concat holds all matches in memory for both the download route and the default text preview (MinIO/S3 branches stream), so any namespace-authorized tenant (or unauthenticated client in standalone) with large objects under a readable prefix can OOM the shared UI pod when GCS is the artifact backend - fork PR open, upstream via private channel (SECURITY.md)

Cross-tenant object-store read via tenant-authored Workflow status in the API server: ResolveArtifactPath (runs/{run}/nodes/{node}/artifacts/{name}:read) and readRunLogFromArchive (v1alpha1 run log archive fallback, enabled by default) take the object key verbatim from status.nodes[*].outputs.artifacts[*].s3.key of the run's stored workflow runtime manifest and fetch it with the API server's own shared object-store credentials, so a multi-user tenant with the edit role (workflows '*', readLog/readArtifact) points a main-logs/artifact key at another namespace's private-artifacts/<ns>/ object or a stored pipeline spec and reads it through their own run; API-server twin of the frontend pod-log fallback issue #152 - fork PR open, upstream via private channel (SECURITY.md)

Credential forwarding in the ml-pipeline-ui TensorBoard proxy: registerTensorboardProxy (frontend/server/handlers/tensorboard-proxy.ts) proxies to the tenant-namespace viewer service with no proxyReq/proxyRes hooks, so the victim's oauth2-proxy session cookie, Authorization bearer token and kubeflow-userid identity header are delivered verbatim to a viewer pod whose image/podTemplateSpec the tenant chooses (POST /apps/tensorboard image= / podtemplatespec=, or a directly created Viewer CR), and viewer Set-Cookie headers are relayed under the UI origin; any co-contributor or admin who opens the viewer leaks a replayable session to the tenant - fork PR open, upstream via private channel (SECURITY.md)

Pre-authentication memory-exhaustion DoS in the KFP API server: buildHTTPRouter (backend/src/apiserver/main.go) proxies every /apis/ request to the grpc-gateway with no body limit (only PUT/PATCH pipeline updates are capped) and startRPCServer sets grpc.MaxRecvMsgSize(math.MaxInt32), so the JSONPb marshaler buffers multi-GB bodies before any TokenReview/SAR; any tenant pod or unauthenticated in-cluster client reaching ml-pipeline:8888/8887 (Istio admits requests without kubeflow-userid) can OOM the shared API server - fork PR open, upstream via private channel (SECURITY.md)

CSRF through the ml-pipeline-ui API proxy: app.ts (frontend/server/app.ts) forwards every /apis/v1beta1|v2beta1/* request and serves POST/DELETE /apps/tensorboard with no origin, Sec-Fetch-Site, custom-header or content-type check, and the API server's MIMEWildcard JSONPb marshaler decodes text/plain form bodies, so a cross-site auto-submitted form carrying the victim's platform session cookie (no SameSite by default: Firefox/Safari, Chrome Lax+POST window) creates runs with an inline pipeline_spec or viewers in the victim's namespace as the victim - fork PR open, upstream via private channel (SECURITY.md)

Cross-tenant pipeline metadata disclosure via namespace-less ListPipelines on the Kubernetes pipeline store: PipelineStoreKubernetes.ListPipelines (backend/src/apiserver/storage/pipeline_store_kubernetes.go) turns the empty namespace of a shared-read request (authorized without SubjectAccessReview by authorizePipelineAccessAndGet) into InNamespace(""), which controller-runtime treats as all namespaces, so any authenticated multi-user caller lists every tenant's Pipeline CRs (names, descriptions, tags, namespaces, ids) when REQUIRE_NAMESPACE_FOR_PIPELINES is unset (default).
